newsitem.title: FRANCE: France sees Thomson debt at 28 bln Ffr.
newsitem.headline: France sees Thomson debt at 28 bln Ffr.

text.p: Electronics group Thomson SA, set to be sold by the government to the Lagardere group, is expected to have 28 billion francs of debt at the end of the year, Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said.
The group's debt stood at 23.8 billion francs at the end of 1995, including 14 billion for the Thomson Multimedia (TMM) unit which Lagardere plans to sell to Daewoo Electronics.
Its debt was expected to rise, as TMM lost three billion francs in the first half of 1996, according to Lagardere.
Arthuis was speaking before the French Senate on Thursday in response to political opposition to the privatisation terms.

The outcry has focused on the sale price of a symbolic one franc to Lagardere, which in turn is selling TV maker TMM to a South Korean company for one franc. Prior to the sale, which must still be approved by the Privatisation Commission, the government plans an 11 billion franc recapitalisation.

"Thomson's debts at the end of 1996 will rise to 28 billion francs and it will have assets of just 21.5 billion," Arthuis said. He said the group's losses since its nationalisation in 1982 will end up totalling 17 billion francs. TMM has lost 10 billion francs since 1988, he added.
